summary: Created one evidence-linked structural copper-scarcity idea. The IEA still projects a material 2035 shortfall, but the gap narrowed as projects advanced, copper investment rose, and recycling offers a real balancing mechanism. Producer evidence supports low-cost operating leverage while also exposing disruption, input-cost, jurisdiction, and capital-intensity risks. Enqueued bounded Southern Copper, Freeport-McMoRan, and Rio Tinto reviews; no relationship, strategy, signal, or paper order was created.

evidence.source: International Energy Agency, Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026
evidence.claim: The IEA projects a roughly 25% copper supply gap in 2035, narrowed from about 30% as projects advanced, and projects copper demand adding about 7 million tonnes by 2040.

evidence.source: International Energy Agency, Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 executive summary
evidence.claim: Copper-focused investment rose 8% in 2025 and secondary supply could roughly double its contribution by 2040, demonstrating meaningful supply-response and recycling counterweights.

Freeport reported treatment charges of USD 2 million versus USD 28 million a year earlier, while its Grasberg ramp delay and higher energy and sulfuric-acid costs demonstrated operational and input-cost offsets to copper pricing.
Freeport's second-quarter release reported USD 2.048 billion of operating cash flow and USD 1.104 billion of capital expenditure while it continued Grasberg restoration and brownfield work.
Southern Copper reported net earnings of USD 1.577 billion, up 67%, and cash cost after by-product credits of negative USD 0.11 per copper pound.
Rio Tinto reported first-half copper-equivalent production up 3%, including more than 30% copper growth at Oyu Tolgoi as the project ramped.
